title: Elucidation and reconstitution of the poplar salicortin biosynthetic pathway
abstract: ) metabolites characteristic of the Salicaceae family. Although salicinoids have long been recognized as effective defense compounds and pharmacologically active constituents in willows and poplars, the biosynthetic pathway underlying their formation remains largely unresolved. Through integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses of black cottonwood (Populus trichocarpa) roots, we identified candidate genes involved in salicinoid biosynthesis belonging to the cytochrome P450 monooxygenase family 92 (CYP92) and the progesterone 5β-reductase/iridoid synthase-like enzyme (PRISE) family of short-chain dehydrogenases/reductases. Co-expression of all identified candidate genes, together with the previously characterized glycosyltransferase gene PtUGT71L1, acyltransferase gene PtACT47, and cinnamic acid-CoA ligase gene PtCNL5, in Nicotiana benthamiana resulted in the production of salicortin, the most abundant salicinoid in poplar. Further characterization of the P450 candidates revealed that two enzymes catalyze ortho-hydroxylation of both aromatic rings of the proposed salicortin precursor, benzyl benzoate, while two other P450s catalyze the subsequent oxidative dearomatization of the benzoic acid-derived ring of benzyl benzoate. The resulting dieneone intermediate is converted by PRISE enzymes via a 1,4-reduction to form the characteristic 1-hydroxy-6-oxocyclohex-2-en-1-carboxylic ester moiety of salicortin. Functional redundancy among the identified CYP92 and PRISE enzymes may reflect the central role of these compounds in plant defense.

title: SpikeFlow-4D maps rice panicle grain-filling kinetics by computed tomography
abstract: Rice yield and grain quality depend on the rate, timing, and uniformity of grain filling, yet the spatial dynamics of this process remain difficult to quantify within intact panicles. Destructive sampling reconstructs developmental trajectories from different plants and cannot directly follow how superior and inferior grains fill within the same organ. Here, we developed SpikeFlow-4D, an in situ 4D CT phenotyping framework for non-destructive, repeated monitoring of rice grain filling. The framework integrates coarse-to-fine segmentation, including slice-wise stem detection and removal, morphological cleaning, DBSCAN-based panicle separation, and grain instance extraction, while retaining original 32-bit reconstructed intensities for gray-value quantification and using 8-bit masks only for intermediate segmentation. Applied to two rice cultivars, 9311 and Zhonghua 11 (ZH11), SpikeFlow-4D quantified temporal changes in mean CT gray value, used as a relative attenuation proxy, across the upper, middle, and lower vertical strata of rice panicles. Logistic modeling of the stratum-level trajectories revealed delayed attenuation increase, a shorter active accumulation period than the upper stratum, and a smaller net attenuation increment in the lower stratum of 9311, whereas the estimated peak increase rate did not differ consistently among strata. At 16 days after flowering, the stratum-level CT gray-value pattern was consistent with independently measured grain fresh weight and was positively associated with dry weight across genotype × stratum group means, without establishing a direct calibration between CT gray value and dry-matter content. These results support SpikeFlow-4D as a non-destructive framework for quantifying spatially resolved, population-level grain-filling dynamics in rice panicles.

title: Integrated Spatial Multi-Omics Reveals Metabolic Hotspots of Paclitaxel Biosynthesis in Taxus yunnanensis
abstract: Paclitaxel (Taxol) is a broad-spectrum anticancer drug, but its clinical application is limited by insufficient production and supply. Although previous studies have noted regional differences in paclitaxel metabolism within stem tissues, the spatial compartmentalization characteristics remain unclear due to the lack of effective analytical methods. Here, we first profiled stem segments of a single Taxus yunnanensis stem spanning six longitudinal positions from juvenile (P1) to mature (P6) tissue by DESI-MSI spatial metabolomics. We then integrated spatial metabolomics with Stereo-seq spatial transcriptomics and single-nucleus RNA-seq at position P2 using three biological replicates, through cross-modality alignment of adjacent sections at the bin level (40 μm). Our findings reveal that intermediate metabolites in the paclitaxel biosynthesis pathway exhibit positive spatial autocorrelation, forming two types of spatial microdomains (metabolic hotspots) with distinct accumulation patterns, one enriched in early scaffold-forming and the other in late side-chain intermediates. Compared with surrounding tissues, these hotspots had relatively higher relative abundancesof paclitaxel intermediates and elevated expression of paclitaxel biosynthesis-related genes, suggesting functional compartmentalization. At hotspot boundaries, ABC transporter genes (such as TyuABCG15) showed higher expression than either inside the hotspots or in the surrounding tissue, suggesting their possible involvement in intercellular transport of paclitaxel intermediates. This study therefore proposes a spatially coordinated multicellular model for paclitaxel biosynthesis, providing new insights into the spatial regulation of plant secondary metabolite biosynthesis and transport.

title: Multi-Layered Regulation of Anthocyanin Biosynthesis: Emerging Mechanisms and Implications for Nutritional and Stress-Resilient Crops
abstract: Anthocyanins are pivotal pigments in plants, imparting vivid coloration and providing substantial nutritional and ecological benefits. While classical reviews have largely focused on biosynthetic enzymes, emerging evidence highlights a multi-layered regulatory architecture that integrates transcriptional control, chromatin state, intracellular transport, hormonal signalling, and environmental cues. In this review, we integrate current knowledge of the MYB-bHLH-WD40 regulatory complex together with emerging mechanisms involving chromatin dynamics, DNA methylation, histone modifications, non-coding RNAs, protein modifications, nutrient signalling, and stress-responsive pathways that collectively fine-tune anthocyanin accumulation. Emphasizing future prospects, we propose anthocyanin-rich plants as strategic targets for enhancing nutritional quality, expanding market value, and improving stress resilience. By synthesizing current breakthroughs and future directions, this review elucidates a comprehensive and forward-looking framework that extends beyond conventional anthocyanin research, aiming to inspire innovative approaches in crop improvement and functional food development.

title: Embodied intelligence for crop production
abstract: Global agriculture faces growing food demand, labor shortages, and climate uncertainty. Although automation has improved agricultural operations, adapting to variable crop states and unstructured environments remains challenging. Embodied intelligence integrates multimodal perception, contextual reasoning, and adaptive action through continuous interaction with crops and their environment. This review examines advances in embodied perception, decision-making, and execution for crop production. We discuss how multimodal sensing, crop growth models, and adaptive control connect individual operations with management objectives across the crop growth cycle. We further identify priorities for system integration, long-term validation, and practical deployment to support precise, sustainable, and resilient food production.
